candidates.statement: This guidance explains how the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) administers the 16 certification process and describes the annual reporting requirements for designated medical 17 gases (DMGs). Specifically, the guidance discusses what products qualify as DMGs, who must 18 submit a certification request, what information must be submitted, and how FDA will evaluate 19 and act on the request. 2

In 189 most cases, the applicant will be the original manufacturer of the gas, that is, the person who 190 initially produces the gas by chemical reaction, physical separation, compression of atmospheric 191 air, or other means. candidates.statement: Any person who seeks to initially introduce or deliver for introduction a DMG into interstate 188 commerce must request a certification as required by § 230.50(a)(1) (21 CFR 230.50(a)(1)). In 189 most cases, the applicant will be the original manufacturer of the gas, that is, the person who 190 initially produces the gas by chemical reaction, physical separation, compression of atmospheric 191 air, or other means. In some instances, original manufacturers may produce gases solely for 192 industrial or other nonmedical uses. Such manufacturers are not subject to the certification 193 requirements in the FD&C Act. However, if a person downstream is the first to market that gas 194 as a medical gas (e.g., after reprocessing an industrial gas into a medical gas for human or animal 195 use), that person must obtain a certification to lawfully market the DMG. 196

candidates.statement: If a DMG certification that has been deemed granted undergoes a change in ownership (e.g., due 405 to a merger or acquisition), an applicant may transfer ownership of the certification. At the time 406 of transfer, the new and former owners are required to submit certain information to FDA. 48 The 407 former owner is required to submit a letter or other document explaining that all rights to the 408 certification have been transferred to the new owner. The new owner is required to submit a 409 supplement under § 230.70 signed by the new owner describing any changes in the conditions in 410 the granted certification, and a letter or other document identifying the date the transfer of 411 ownership is effective. 412

WITHDRAWAL OR REVOCATION OF APPROVAL 441

candidates.statement: Under § 230.150(a)(3), FDA will withdraw approval of an application if the applicant requests 458 the withdrawal because the DMG subject to the application is no longer being marketed, 459 provided none of the conditions listed in § 230.150(a)(1) and (2) apply. An applicant that wishes 460 to withdraw its application should submit a new Form FDA 3864 and check Other as the type of 461 submission. In the text box, the applicant should note that they are submitting a withdrawal 462 request. FDA will send an acknowledgement letter to the applicant upon receipt of the request 463 for withdrawal. FDA will consider the withdrawal request to be a waiver of an opportunity for 464 hearing, and such withdrawal would be without prejudice to refiling. 465

If the applicant agrees, FDA will not make a finding 471 under § 230.150(a)(1) or (2), but will withdraw approval of the application in a notice published 472 in the Federal Register that contains a brief summary of FDA’s and the applicant’s views of the 473 reasons for withdrawal. 474
